meaning: to hit; to play (a ball game)
conceptZh: 玩具機器人擺出全壘打架式，使盡全力揮棒——球紋風不動地掉在地上，飛出去的是球棒；球棒直直插進地面變成「丁」，三塊積木滑過來排成提手旁，合成「打」。
object: a toy robot batter, a chunky bat and a ball
morph: the flying bat lands upright as the 丁 on the right while three bricks slide in to form the 扌 radical on the left of 打
creativeAngle: 接著足球再加上打擊運動：笑點是「球沒動、棒子飛了」的預期落差，而飛出去的球棒直立插地，本身就是丁那一豎一鉤，動作與筆劃完全對上。打只有五畫，適合做真正的組裝。語音詞「打球」，打在此念ㄉㄚˇ、球ㄑㄧㄡˊ都已在字庫，避開一打的ㄉㄚˊ。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid light cream background. Centered stands a stubby toy robot batter in an oversized helmet, gripping a chunky wooden bat, with a soft ball hovering on a tee in front of him. From 0.6 seconds he winds up with colossal commitment, shoulders coiling, helmet slipping over his eyes. At 1.8 seconds he swings with everything he has. The ball does not move at all; it simply drops off the tee and rolls a few centimetres. The bat, however, flies out of his hands, spins once through the air, and at 2.6 seconds plants itself upright in the ground to the right of centre with a solid thunk, its handle hooking at the base. The robot pushes his helmet up and stares at it. At 3.2 seconds three chunky bricks slide in from the left and stack into a hand-shaped radical beside the standing bat. He shrugs, picks up the ball, and hops out of frame to the left by 4.4 seconds. By 4.8 seconds everything has resolved into one correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 打 in saturated deep cobalt blue, perfectly centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height with generous margins, its left 扌 radical and right 丁 clearly separated and every stroke and hook crisp. From 4.9 to 8.0 seconds the frame holds completely still on 打 with nothing else moving in the shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「打、打、打球」, using the reading ㄉㄚˇ for 打 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 打 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 打球 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 打: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.
